topic: Pop quiz: when did the last woolly mammoths die out?
notes: Options: A) before the first farms (~10,000 years ago), B) after the Great Pyramid of Giza was built, C) during the Roman Empire. Answer B: a small population survived on Wrangel Island (Arctic Ocean) until about 4,000 years ago (~2000 BC); the Great Pyramid dates to ~2560 BC. Most mainland mammoths were gone ~10,000 years ago, which is why A is the common guess. Sources to check: Dalén et al., Cell 2024 (Wrangel genomes), Vartanyan et al. 1993 Nature, Smithsonian / Live Science / Natural History Museum. Say 'about 4,000 years ago', not an exact year. Plausibility check 9/11: WorldAtlas and Business Insider (Cell 2024 study) both support it. Hook (statement style, B1 variant) must NOT give the answer away, e.g. 'The last mammoths died shockingly recently. Pop quiz: when?' Ticking clock = wifi_objects:clock or code. ancient_person = Egyptian builders (pyramids reel). Category history: rotation after nature (8/11). Format quiz: fewest reels with versus/what_if, used longest ago (1/11).

topic: Bone vs steel: which is really stronger?
notes: 3 rounds, same units on both sides: 1) raw strength (MPa; steel wins: structural steel ~250+ MPa yield vs cortical bone ~130-200 MPa in compression), 2) weight (density g/cm3; bone ~1.9 vs steel ~7.8, bone wins), 3) self-repair (bone heals itself, steel can't; bone wins). Twist: pound for pound bone is about as strong as (or stronger than) mild steel, and it rebuilds itself. Final 2-1 bone. Check exact figures and avoid the loose 'bone is 5x stronger than steel' claim unless a solid source states it. Sources to check: Ansys blog 'Is bone material stronger than steel?', Discover Magazine, Britannica (bone, steel), a biomechanics textbook/review. scientist explains; young_man for the x-ray / everyday body. Category body: next in rotation. Format versus: tie with what_if, used longest ago (3/11). Goosebumps (only body reel) had the weakest hook hold: keep the first 3 s very visual (bone vs steel bar side by side, something moving at frame 0).
